TECH2_2021-1.exp: Good governance is defined as citizen-centric: the citizen is the customer and ultimate stakeholder whose service experience measures whether governance is good. Efficiency and organisation are means, and the ARC is merely a reform body, not the core.

TECH2_2021-2.exp: A Citizens' Charter must be non-discriminatory (equal service standards for all users) and must set out the grievance/complaint redress mechanism, both being standard mandatory components. Both statements are therefore true.

TECH2_2021-3.exp: ICT's recognised structural impacts are easier access to information, online service delivery, and improved intra- and inter-governmental transactions. Centralization of services is the trap: ICT typically enables decentralised, distributed delivery (CSCs, e-District) rather than centralising it, so 'All of them' is wrong.

TECH2_2021-4.exp: The standard UNDP/UN-ESCAP attributes of good governance include transparency, responsiveness and accountability (with participation, rule of law, equity, consensus and effectiveness). Democracy is a form of political system, not itself listed as a property of good governance, so 'All of the above' is the trap.

TECH2_2021-5.exp: Audit of the accounts of both the Union and the States is a Union List entry, discharged by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India. States cannot legislate on or control the audit of their own accounts, which is what makes it a union subject rather than a state or concurrent one.

TECH2_2021-6.exp: The four standard e-Governance interaction domains are G2C, G2B, G2G and G2E, all of which are government-initiated. C2G is not part of that canonical set, though some wider taxonomies do describe citizen-to-government flows, which is why the printed list is a little loose.

TECH2_2021-7.exp: Adopting the right approach (right scoping, right delivery model, right sequencing) is treated as the essential precondition for an e-Governance project, while a business model, configuration management and stakeholder impact are outputs or supporting activities within it. This question is weakly worded and more than one option is arguably defensible, so treat it as uncertain.

TECH2_2021-8.exp: Identifying IT-enablement opportunities and drawing up requirements belongs to the Future State Definition phase, where the To-Be process is designed and the system requirements flow from it. Current State Assessment only documents the As-Is position; the develop-and-implement phase acts on requirements already defined.

TECH2_2021-9.exp: Current State (As-Is) Assessment yields process maps, pain points and an analysis of strengths and gaps. A data digitization strategy is a forward-looking design decision produced in the future-state/implementation planning phase, not a product of documenting what exists today.

TECH2_2021-10.exp: The Delphi technique gathers anonymous, iterative rounds of expert opinion until consensus emerges, and is the classic tool for securing expert judgement. WBS is a scope-decomposition tool and peer review checks work products, not forecasts.

TECH2_2021-11.exp: Project management doctrine holds that individual development, both managerial and technical, is the foundation on which team development is built. Motivation and conflict management are practices applied within an already-forming team.

TECH2_2021-12.exp: At project closure the complete indexed set of project records is placed in the project archive for future reference and audit. A project report is only one document within that set, not the repository.

TECH2_2021-13.exp: CV = EV - AC and SV = EV - PV, so a positive value on each means earned value exceeds both actual cost and planned value: under budget and ahead of schedule. The trap is reading 'positive variance' as overspending; positive is always favourable in earned value analysis.

TECH2_2021-14.exp: A vision statement is qualitative and aspirational, describing the conditions and ambitions the organisation wants to reach. It is not quantifiable and does not derive from business strategy, since strategy is formulated to realise the vision, not the other way round.

TECH2_2021-15.exp: Permits, along with licences and certificates, are classic Government-to-Citizen transactions. Career enhancement and professional education fall under G2E (employee-facing), while filing of returns is typically classified under G2B taxation services.

TECH2_2021-16.exp: Parallel adoption runs the legacy and new systems side by side, so the old system remains a working fallback and errors are caught by comparison, making it the least risky though the most costly. Big Bang, with no fallback, is the riskiest.

TECH2_2021-17.exp: PBC in tendering stands for Pre-Bid Conference, the meeting where bidders seek clarifications on the RFP before submitting bids, and whose minutes are issued as corrigenda. The other expansions are not procurement terms.

TECH2_2021-18.exp: e-Governance change management is explicitly people, process and technology together: it alters operational routines, introduces new technology, and must shift the attitudes and behaviour of staff. Restricting it to any one dimension is the standard misconception.

TECH2_2021-19.exp: In the citizen-experience framing used in e-governance material, having to make repeated visits to a government office is the textbook symptom of poor governance and the pain point e-governance is designed to remove. The question is defective because corrupt officers is equally a sign of poor governance; option B (service as a right) describes good governance.

TECH2_2021-20.exp: The four GPR stages run problem identification and definition, process analysis of the As-Is, process re-engineering into the To-Be, and finally process implementation, so the fourth is implementation. Frameworks that split the analysis stage further would shift this, which is why the answer depends on the four-step model the options imply.
